Unfortunately, the relationship was brief, as Thomas was called back to the US in the waning days of the war, with little time for goodbyes. Subsequently, they wrote to each other for some time, but the separation posed too much of a strain for them to bear.Back in America, Thomas continued his correspondence with Morris and finally proposed to her to come back to America and marry him. She misinterpreted the letter and took it as Thomas having met someone else. Therefore, she refused, saying that she was becoming a nurse in Britain. The misunderstanding was left unresolved, and the letters stopped. Both married other people. Morris went to Australia with her husband, and Thomas stayed with his wife in America. Morris divorced her husband approximately 30 years after her marriage, while Thomas remained with his wife until she died in 2001.Though time had elapsed, neither had completely forgotten the relationship. Morris was said to have had a picture of Thomas and stared at it for years after the war. Thomas said that he remembered her and that she stayed in his mind long after they parted. The chance of rekindling their romance arose in 2015 when Morris showed her son a photograph of Thomas and asked him to look on the Internet. Finally, her son Robert located his name in a newspaper clipping of the D-Day landing in The Virginian-Pilot. Their chance reunion, over 70 years after they had last seen each other, commenced with a telephone call and a shared Skype video call with members of both their families. The conversation brought back memories of what they had shared.After years of reestablishing the relationship with Thomas, the pair finally arranged to meet face to face. At 93, Thomas was due to leave Virginia Beach and travel over 10,000 miles to Adelaide. The story of their reunion was picked up by the media around the world, and hundreds of people contributed to an online fundraising page.Air New Zealand organised a free upgrade to first class for Thomas and his son Steve, helping them make the long journey. The flight was scheduled for February 2016, with Thomas arriving at the airport on 11 February. Nervous as he was, he was happy he would be able to see the woman he remembered for most of his life.The couple’s reunion was emotional. They hugged, they kissed, and Thomas said he was glad he had finally been able to see Morris again. The meeting was covered by Australian broadcaster ABC and other news outlets. Thomas spent a couple of weeks with his former love in Adelaide on Valentine's Day, and their reunion did not erase the years they had spent apart, but it did give them a chance to revisit unfinished parts of their lives.
Article Summary: Norwood Thomas met Joyce Durrant Morris in London in 1944 when she was 17 and he was 21. Their brief romance was cut short when he was deployed to the war front. They wrote to each other for some time, but the separation posed too much of a strain for them to bear. Morris divorced her husband approximately 30 years after her marriage, while Thomas remained with his wife until she died in 2001.

Article Title: On Minnesota’s I-35W bridge, road sensors and a weather system detected conditions that could lead to ice, then triggered spray heads to distribute potassium acetate across the deck; an evaluation rep
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing an automated bridge anti-icing system spraying potassium acetate across the bridge. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

Why the I-35W bridge was vulnerable to winter accidents

How the automated anti-icing technology works

Minneapolis has implemented a cutting-edge anti-icing system on Interstate 35W to significantly improve road safety during winter months. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

The 68% reduction in crashes and its wider implications

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A bridge in Minnesota shows how technology can help prevent icy driving conditions before roads become unsafe. A smart anti-icing system installed on Interstate 35W in Minneapolis releases a chemical agent across the bridge before temperatures drop and ice forms. The system was made to prevent ice rather than simply clean it.An operational evaluation by the Minnesota Department of Transportation found that the method prevented 68% of non-dry crashes during evaluation, demonstrating the promise of automated road treatments to enhance winter driving safety. The system was installed on the I-35W bridge over the Mississippi River, where freezing conditions presented frequent challenges to travellers. Its proximity, heavy use, and exposure to the elements made the bridge especially susceptible to black ice, a transparent, smooth sheet of ice that often goes unnoticed by drivers.The I-35W bridge was chosen for this effort because of its record of winter crashes. A July 2001 operational evaluation reported that the bridge carried about 139,000 vehicles a day in 2000. Situated over the Mississippi River, the area was also exposed to moisture from industrial plants at Saint Anthony Falls and passing cars, creating conditions that could lead to ice formation.So drivers might have found themselves driving on slippery roads, potentially losing control of their vehicle more often than they anticipated, particularly during slower rush hours or periods of frequent congestion. To help combat this, road salt like sodium chloride was already being used for winter road maintenance. And now the bridge needed to be equipped with a system that could detect the onset of these potentially hazardous situations as soon as possible and treat them effectively.The system takes information from two kinds of pavement sensors to gauge conditions where ice might form. These consist of temperature and moisture sensors. In addition, the system includes ice-detection sensors and a road weather information system that measures temperature and rain, sleet, and snow. This information is communicated to a computer system at MnDOT’s dispatch centre approximately five miles from the bridge. When the combined readings suggest danger is imminent, the computer initiates the appropriate spraying program. Leaks are then checked before the spray equipment is powered up.Flashing yellow warning lights at the intersection advise motorists that the system is active. The system is made up of 38-valve units linked to 76 spray nozzles on the bridge deck. Potassium acetate is sprayed from each nozzle in a fan-shaped pattern to disseminate the liquid across the whole width of the highway. Rather than dispensing the entire supply at once, the computer releases the solution in sections based on readings. The actual spraying cycle takes 10 to 12 minutes, with each nozzle transmitting the solution for just over 2 seconds.Potassium acetate was chosen as a de-icer because it is effective at low temperatures and is much less damaging to the structure and reinforcing steel than typical chloride-based de-icers. It is environmentally friendly and contains no chloride, which is found in typical road salt. Furthermore, the research published in Accident Analysis and Prevention examined how ice detection sensors could help transportation agencies monitor road conditions, improve driver awareness, and support automated anti-icing systems.The performance of the installation was also evaluated during two winter seasons of operational testing. The evaluation examined results from the 2000 to 2001 winter season and compared them with the results from the 1996 to 1997 winter season. The latter was selected because the weather conditions were similar to those in 2000 and 2001. The analysis indicated that non-dry crashes were reduced to 31 in comparison to 10 in the test winter. This indicated that the 68% reduction in non-dry winter crashes occurred.The assessment also disclosed a benefit-to-cost ratio of 3.4, signifying that the projected benefit will surpass the cost of installation, upkeep, and chemical supply. The initial installation cost was about $578,365, and the adjusted final cost was $618,450.10. Further testing revealed problems with upkeep, as a few spray nozzles clogged with solid ice and snow during ploughing, and the chemical also sprayed in excess onto the bridge deck.This indicates that routine maintenance and correct positioning of the spray were necessary.The system’s environmental advantages also require careful consideration, although potassium acetate does not add chloride. Research published by the University of Minnesota found that too high a concentration could be harmful to aquatic life, suggesting the chemical should be used selectively rather than broadly. Thus, the I-35W project ultimately showed how monitoring the weather using pavement sensors and automating the application of chemicals can work to avoid the winter road black ice problem. Its results also provided transportation agencies with an example of how to use technology to improve safety at bridges where standard winter maintenance is difficult.
Article Summary: The I-35W bridge was chosen for this effort because of its record of winter crashes. Potassium acetate was chosen as a de-icer because it is effective at low temperatures and is much less damaging to the structure and reinforcing steel than typical chloride-based de-icers. It is environmentally friendly and contains no chloride, which is found in typical road salt.

Article Title: At two North Dakota bridge sites, pavement and weather sensors detected conditions that could produce ice and automatically triggered fixed nozzles to spray deicer; evaluations reported 50–66% fewer c
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing workers inspecting and operating an automated bridge deicing system, which sprays liquid deicer onto a winter road to prevent ice formation and improve driving safety. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

Why bridge decks become dangerous during winter

How a sensor-based spray system prevents ice formation

North Dakota has successfully deployed an innovative anti-icing system known as Fixed Automated Spray Technology to improve the safety of its roads. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

Crash reductions and the challenges of automated treatment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When the weather is wintry, bridges can be treacherous, even if other roads are mostly thawed out. In 2007, North Dakota automated a new road system that helped reduce how pavement sensors and computer-controlled spray equipment can pre-empt such hazards before ice forms. Named Fixed Automated Spray Technology (FAST), the system continuously measures pavement and air temperature and dispenses anti-icing chemical in anticipation of freezing.An evaluation of two installations by researchers at North Dakota State University found that the technology cut crashes by 50% to 66% at the bridge locations where it was installed, which may offer a useful option for roads that experience repeated winter crashes. NDDOT began work on the project after finding bridges where crashes frequently occurred during winter weather. The project had two installations: one on I-29 near Buxton and another on the I-94 Red River Bridge at the North Dakota-Minnesota border near Moorhead, Minnesota. These installations showed how automated maintenance equipment could help transportation agencies react better to changing road conditions without waiting for the crew.Bridge decks can become icy more quickly than adjoining roads because they are exposed to cold air from both above and below, allowing their surfaces to lose heat rapidly.As a result, moisture from rain or snow can freeze on a bridge even when nearby road surfaces remain relatively safe. This difference in the surface conditions can catch motorists off guard, increasing the risk of skidding and collision. According to the evaluation of North Dakota Fixed Automated Spray Technology (FAST) systems, the Buxton and Red River bridges were selected because of their history of winter-related crashes. The Buxton Bridge system became operational in December 2002, while the Red River Bridge system began operating in 2007. This first installation covers 370 feet of roadway and bridge deck, including approximately 330 feet of bridge deck. The second one extends across 2,300 feet of roadway, of which 1,300 feet consists of bridge decking.The FAST installation contains pavement sensors, environmental sensor stations, and computer-controlled spray equipment. Pavement sensors provide continuous monitoring of surface temperature and moisture and can tell whether the roadway surface is dry or wet and what the freezing point of any liquid present is. The other environmental monitoring equipment provides extra data, such as temperature, dew point, wind speed, and rate of precipitation. When the data from the sensors hit a threshold indicating the potential for frost, freezing, or precipitation, the system fires a command to the spray equipment. This system fires a command to the spray equipment to dispense a liquid anti-icing solution on the bridge deck.The solution lowers the moisture’s freezing point on the surface, which can help prevent ice formation and adhesion to the pavement. Both systems use what is known as CryoTech CF7, an anti-icing solution that is made of potassium acetate. According to a 2009 study by North Dakota State University researchers Shawn Birst and Mohammad Smadi, the anti-icing solution was chosen for its low-temperature performance and reduced structural damage. The equipment also allows maintenance personnel to monitor conditions remotely and to initiate preventive measures when necessary. Research published in the Canadian Journal of Civil Engineering has highlighted the importance of reliable environmental sensors, appropriate installation locations, and regular maintenance for the successful operation of FAST systems.North Dakota’s installation results were analysed with crash data from 12 winter seasons, January 1996 to May 2008, and compared crash rates before and after the system was installed, leaving out crashes caused by things the technology could not impact, such as animals or rocks on the road. At Buxton Bridge, the average crashes per winter season decreased from 6.2 before the system was installed to 2.5 after, a 59% reduction. Adjusted for changes in average daily traffic counts, the reduction was 66% for property damage crashes, 62% for injury crashes, and 75% for fatalities.The Red River Bridge also improved, with a total drop in crashes on the North Dakota side; after traffic adjustments, crash totals dropped 55%. On the Minnesota side, they dropped overall 46%. The total on both sides dropped about 50%. The system was estimated to be at least 95% effective, though its use was limited. For example, spraying was halted when the wind speed hit 15 miles per hour because high winds could cause the mist to blow off the roadway, and the equipment was shut down when road temperature fell below 12 degrees Fahrenheit because keeping the mist effective would require much more of the chemical.Financial reviews provided an additional silver lining. At Buxton, the benefit-to-cost ratio was 4.3, while for Red River it was 1.3 over 20 years. The benefit calculation included the decreased cost of congestion and maintenance. The team showed how automated de-icing technology could complement traditional winter road maintenance, particularly at bridges that tend to attract a lot of accidents in winter.
Article Summary: Bridge decks can become icy more quickly than adjoining roads because they are exposed to cold air from both above and below. North Dakota has successfully deployed an innovative anti-icing system known as Fixed Automated Spray Technology to improve the safety of its roads. An evaluation of two installations by researchers at North Dakota State University found that the technology cut crashes by 50% to 66% at the bridge locations.

Article Title: A Cuban father of a US-born child was detained by immigration officers in Kentucky for nearly six months; a November 10 federal ruling found his detention unlawful and ordered his immediate release
Article Text:
Cuban father was detained by US immigration officers for nearly six months. (AI image)

How ICE brought Castellano back into custody

Why court rejected government's argument

ICE directed to release him immediately

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Cuban man detained by US immigration authorities for nearly six months must be released immediately, a federal court in Kentucky ruled on Tuesday. The court found that officials had failed to follow the required legal process before keeping him in custody, violating his constitutional right to due process.The ruling available on Justia , concerns Damichel Jesus Viamontes Castellano, who was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers on May 19. He had earlier been taken into custody by US Border Patrol agents in Texas in 2022 but was allowed to remain outside detention while his immigration case proceeded.Castellano has since been held at the Oldham County Detention Center in La Grange, Kentucky. His immigration case took another turn on July 28, when an immigration judge directed that he be removed to Cuba. However, he challenged that decision, and his appeal is still being considered by the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA).The pending appeal was important to the court's decision because the removal order had not yet become administratively final. The judge also noted that both sides agreed that Castellano's detention fell under Section 1226(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act. This provision allows immigration authorities to hold a person while deciding whether they should be removed from the country.Castellano has family and business connections in Kentucky. He is the father of a child born in Louisville in 2024 who is a US citizen. His mother is also a lawful permanent resident and has an approved family petition filed on his behalf. He runs an active Kentucky business, as its sole organiser and registered agent.According to the court, officials had not properly assessed whether he needed to remain in custody or informed him of the procedure available to challenge that decision.Castellano first came to the attention of US immigration authorities in 2022, when Border Patrol agents arrested him in Texas. He was issued a notice to appear in immigration proceedings and subsequently released on his own recognisance.ICE revisited his case in May. Officers found that he had earlier received the immigration notice and had faced charges of DUI and reckless driving in February 2025. These charges prompted the agency to plan a targeted operation to take him into custody.ICE arrested him on May 19 and withdrew the release granted to him in 2022. Officials issued several immigration documents, including a warrant of arrest, but did not give him Form I-286, the notice used to communicate an initial custody decision.That missing document became central to the court proceedings. It allows a detained person to understand the government's decision and seek a review by an immigration judge, including a hearing to request release on bond.The court found no record showing that ICE had considered Castellano's individual circumstances before deciding to detain him. Under the applicable rules, officers must examine whether a person is likely to attend future immigration hearings and whether their release would create a safety risk.The judge also found that the government had not established that Castellano received the required information about his detention or how he could challenge it.The government maintained that Castellano should have approached the immigration court himself to seek a fresh decision on his custody. Its lawyers argued that he could have filed a request for a bond hearing rather than approaching the federal court directly.Castellano argued that immigration officials had failed to complete the initial steps required by their own rules and could not shift the responsibility to him after leaving those steps unfinished.The federal judge accepted this argument. The court found that the authorities had not carried out the initial custody review or provided the necessary notice. It therefore declined to make Castellano complete another administrative process before considering his challenge.The judge also considered the time he had already spent in custody. By the time he approached the court, he had remained detained for more than 120 days without an independent judicial examination of the decision to keep him there.The ruling further addressed the responsibility of proving whether detention was necessary. The government wanted the detained person to demonstrate that they were neither a danger to the community nor likely to flee.The court disagreed with this approach. It held that the government must establish through clear and convincing evidence that a person presents a danger or flight risk during a bond hearing under Section 1226(a).In explaining its position, the judge pointed to the difficulties faced by people in immigration detention. They may struggle to collect documents and evidence, understand complicated immigration procedures or obtain legal assistance. The court said these difficulties made it important for the government to justify continued detention.It also considered Castellano's earlier release. ICE had allowed him to remain outside custody after his 2022 arrest but later decided to detain him again. The court found that the government had not shown why keeping him confined without the required review was justified.The judge concluded that the failure to assess Castellano's case individually and inform him of his right to challenge detention had deprived him of due process under the Fifth Amendment to the US Constitution.The court also considered the impact of detention on personal freedom and the government's reasons for holding him. It found that immigration authorities had not established a sufficient basis for continuing his confinement without following the prescribed safeguards.It consequently granted his petition for a writ of habeas corpus, along with his request to expedite the proceedings.The ruling also places conditions on any attempt to detain him again. Unless circumstances have materially changed, officials must first provide him with a bond hearing under Section 1226(a).
Article Summary: Damichel Jesus Viamontes Castellano was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers on May 19. He had earlier been taken into custody by US Border Patrol agents in Texas in 2022 but was allowed to remain outside detention while his immigration case proceeded. His immigration case took another turn on July 28, when an immigration judge directed that he be removed to Cuba. He challenged that decision, and his appeal is still being considered by the Board of Immigration Appeals.

Article Title: In 1942, Army Air Corps serviceman Raymond Brim went AWOL for nearly 48 hours to marry Pat before shipping overseas; their daughter passed on Pat’s wartime letters 77 years later
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image of a young woman writing a letter to her husband serving overseas during World War II. Image credits: ChatGPT

A wedding before leaving the country for overseas duties

Letters exchanged across the Atlantic as Raymond flew combat

missions

Representative image of soldiers reading letters from their friends and family. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A daughter’s decision to pass on the letters

On February 14, 1944, 20-year-old Patricia Brim sent her husband, Raymond, a photograph which accompanied a letter from home. In the letter, she playfully described the pose in the picture and mentioned that she wished to continue sending him pictures so that he would never forget her. This letter was part of the exchange that documented the couple’s separation during the Second World War. Raymond Brim served with the US Army Air Corps in Europe, in which he carried out bombing missions against the Nazis.Prior to his overseas posting, Raymond had taken an extraordinary step to marry Patricia. As he was unable to obtain leave from his air base in Wyoming, he went absent without leave (AWOL) and travelled to Utah for the wedding. He was away from his post for nearly 48 hours, according to The Washington Post. A subsequent profile from the University of Utah revealed that he was away for three days as his crew covered for him.During his late teens, Raymond Brim had been studying at the University of Utah and working in a mine. The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, however, changed his plans. According to the university profile, Brim left his studies and enlisted in the Army Air Corps. After completing his training, he was awaiting assignment to join his combat group in England and fly the B-17 Flying Fortress.But before the assignment, he wanted to marry Patricia, whom he had met on a blind date.While the couple had expected a small wedding, Patricia’s former school’s headmistress, however, reportedly arranged for the entire student body of Rowland Hall in Salt Lake City to walk to St. Mark’s Episcopal Cathedral to attend the wedding in December 1942. The university’s account describes the wedding as a pit stop before Raymond’s deployment in England.Letters and pictures became an important way to communicate for the couple once Raymond was deployed overseas. One of Patricia’s surviving messages was written ahead of Christmas 1943, in which she recalled their previous Christmas together, including a meal, a decorated tree and attending church in the snow. She expressed that she missed him and hoped that they would be able to spend the next Christmas together.By the time Patricia sent her Valentine’s Day photograph in 1944, Raymond had already been flying missions over Europe. The University of Utah profile reports that he served with a special unit of the 482nd Bomb Group . The unit’s aircraft reportedly used the Pathfinder radar guidance system. The technology helped bomber crews navigate and identify targets when cloud cover made visibility difficult. The 482nd was formed particularly to provide radar-equipped Pathfinder aircraft for the Eighth Air Force’s bombing formations.Raymond reportedly completed 25 combat missions and received the Distinguished Flying Cross and four Air Medals. Following his final mission, he was assigned to train new pilots. His daughter, Celia Straus, recalled in an interview that her father had promised himself he would return home to Patricia. He came back to her after surviving the war, and they remained married for 65 years before Patricia died in 2007. Raymond died in 2019, as noted by The Washington Post.After her parents’ death, Straus inherited a folder filled with her mother’s correspondence. In February 2021, she handed her mother’s letters to historian Andrew Carroll, whom she had known for years through their work on veteran support projects.Notably, Carroll had been collecting wartime correspondence since 1989, when a family member gave him a letter written during World War II . What had begun as a single document soon expanded into a collection of more than 100,000 letters from American conflicts. With The Washington Post, he shared that letters written by women to their husbands were considered particularly valuable because servicemen were often unable to bring their wives’ correspondence home. Therefore, the survival of these letters from Patricia added a women’s perspective to the record of wartime correspondence.
Article Summary: Raymond Brim served with the US Army Air Corps in Europe, in which he carried out bombing missions against the Nazis. Prior to his overseas posting, Raymond had taken an extraordinary step to marry Patricia. As he was unable to obtain leave from his air base in Wyoming, he went absent without leave (AWOL) and travelled to Utah for the wedding.

Article Title: A 4,000-year-old wall, an ancient bank and a ditch emerged from Morocco’s Oued Beht ridge, clarifying a puzzle first recorded in 1936
Article Text:
A representative AI image of ancient stone walls, excavated enclosures and a deep ditch. (Image Credits: ChatGPT)

Who were they keeping out?

A bustling gathering point of Northwest Africa

Representative image of an archaeological excavation. (Image Credits: Pexels)

Clues beneath the surface and across the sea

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Researchers uncovered a previously unknown chapter of history after discovering a large-scale construction at Oued Beht in 2023. It lies in North Africa beyond the Nile Valley, and researchers estimated it to be about 4,000 to 3,500 years old. According to the research paper titled “Expanding Oued Beht: Final Neolithic, Bronze Age, medieval and later discoveries from excavation and survey in 2023” , the construction was likely used as a defensive structure. But against what or whom is not yet determined. Prior to this discovery, researchers at the Oued Beht Archaeological Project had already established two things. Firstly, the agricultural complex was likely the largest and earliest in Africa outside the Nile Valley, as per a 2024 report in The Conversation by archaeologists Cyprian Broodbank, Giulio Lucarini and Youssef Bokbot. Secondly, its inception was dated to between 3400 BCE and 2900 BCE, per the same report. The paper says six new trenches were opened in 2023, including a 5 × 5 m exposure beside earlier French-Moroccan excavations, and that Trench 3/3.1 was crucial for untangling “Wall B1.” In that trench, the team identified prehistoric foundations for a daub-and-possibly-stone wall, a later stone-built wall above it, a multi-phased embankment and a parallel ditch, with radiocarbon dates and prehistoric pottery used to refine the sequence.In 1936, French archaeologist Armand Ruhlmann recorded three walls crossing the Oued Beht ridge in northwest Morocco, as reported in the research paper. He interpreted them as a defensive barrier, but their age remained uncertain. In 2023, after new excavations at the site, researchers deepened their knowledge of the region. The findings come from the Oued Beht Archaeological Project’s third field season. The team examined Wall B1, the largest of four built alignments in the ridge’s southern section, which differs from the three walls Ruhlmann recorded. What appeared to be one substantial wall proved to be several features, including wall foundations, an earthen embankment and a ditch. Studying the sites gave researchers the vantage point of looking at the everyday rural life of prehistoric and medieval times, often overlooked by history books.Researchers opined the wall may have been built to safeguard land and resources from rival neighbours rather than foreign invaders, though the exact threat remained elusive. The wall may also have served to exert control and power. Local communities wanted to stake their claim on important locations and leverage the mobility of those who passed through the area. The wall suggested that organised defence in the Maghreb was much older and more complex than researchers previously thought. As per the study, people had returned to the exact ridge at Oued Beht between the 11th and 13th centuries CE and rebuilt the wall. Along with it, they had also established a small village on the top of a hill and sandwiched a cemetery right between the village and the wall.Up to this point, little was known about the ancient history of the Maghreb, which now comprises Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia. Between 3400 and 2900 BCE, Oued Beht was a hub of farming and craft-making. The people who used the site farmed barley and wheat, raised livestock, and were major producers of stone axes and painted pots. However, researchers were unsure if these people actually lived there or were just visitors. This suggests northwest Morocco may have been a regional meeting point.In the 1930s, archaeologists had noticed old linear walls and embankments at Oued Beht, but they did not know their age until the recent excavation, as per the paper. After radiocarbon dating of the deposits, researchers posited the timelines for the ditches, embankments and walls. As per the results, they were built during the Bronze Age. This may make them among the oldest defensive structures in North Africa outside of Egypt.Moreover, the communities in the region did not live in isolation, as believed. Across the water, between 2200 and 1550 BCE, people in Southern Spain and Portugal, known as Argaric societies, were pioneering complex infrastructure and planned towns on hilltops. The hallmark of their work was characterised by advanced metallurgy, particularly bronze production. Because communities in northwest Africa (Oued Beht) lived in the same parallel timeline as their European counterparts, researchers compared their fortified hilltop settlements. This may help explain the defensive wall system built on a strategic ridge at Oued Beht. Following another trail of clues in the deep storage pits helped researchers establish another link between North Africa and Europe. The same types of pits used for storing food or goods were found in Iberia during that period, The Conversation reported.
Article Summary: Oued Beht was a hub of farming and craft-making between 3400 and 2900 BCE. It lies in North Africa beyond the Nile Valley, and researchers estimated it to be about 4,000 to 3,500 years old. The construction was likely used as a defensive structure, but against what or whom is not yet determined.

Article Title: 74 militants killed in Pakistan security operations along Afghan border in 10 days
Article Text:
43 militants killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa raids, 31 in Balochistan operations: Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistani security forces have killed 74 militants in a series of raids and operations in the country's northwest and southwest regions bordering Afghanistan over the past 10 days, the Associated Press cited military officials Friday.The raids were conducted in Mir Ali and Orakzai districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where troops killed 43 militants and recovered weapons, ammunition and explosive devices, the military said in a statement.Separately, security forces killed 31 militants in multiple operations in Balochistan province since November 3, the military said. The province has been witnessing a bloody insurgency led by the rebel Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).Kabul has denied accusations of providing support to militant groups operating against Pakistan.The Pakistani Taliban are a separate group from, but allied with, Afghanistan's Taliban, who returned to power in Kabul in 2021. Several TTP leaders and fighters are believed to be operating from sanctuaries across the Afghan border, a longstanding source of tension between Islamabad and Kabul.
Article Summary: Pakistani security forces have killed 74 militants in a series of raids and operations in the country's northwest and southwest regions bordering Afghanistan. The raids were conducted in Mir Ali and Orakzai districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Separately, security forces killed 31 militants in multiple operations in Balochistan province since November 3.

Article Title: BLA claims 18 killed in suicide vehicle attack on Pakistan Army camp in Balochistan
Article Text:
Baloch Liberation Army claims responsibility for a suicide vehicle attack on a Pakistani Army camp in Balochistan, claiming 18 personnel were killed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Multiple casualties were reported in a VBIED attack at Pak army’s main camp in Mastung, Balochistan Thursday. The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) took responsibility for the attack, claiming to have eliminated 18 personnel.According to BLA, its Fidayeen attack, the Majeed Brigade, carried out an operation in the Kanak area of Mastung, targeting a Pakistani military camp with a suicide vehicle-borne improvised explosive device followed by an assault by its armed fighters who entered the premises and targeted military personnel.The attack unfolded while a meeting of senior Pak Army personnel including colonel rank officials was underway when the mini-truck laden with explosives rammed into the main gate of the camp.The area has been on the boil since Wednesday. According to pro-BLA accounts on Telegram, Pak security forces were carrying out “operation Radd-ul-Fitna”, aimed at destroying tunnels allegedly made by Baloch rebels, on Wednesday and Thursday in the area.They claimed to have destroyed seven tunnels and seized arms, ammunition and explosives. In Musakhel, unidentified set ablaze construction machinery and a separate explosion destroyed a bridge in Mastung.On Wednesday, 13 Pakistani police personnel including a Deputy Superintendent of Police were killed after fighters from the rebel group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) launched a major attack targeting mobile police units in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Article Summary: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) took responsibility for the attack, claiming to have eliminated 18 personnel. The attack unfolded while a meeting of senior Pak Army personnel including colonel rank officials was underway when the mini-truck laden with explosives rammed into the main gate of the camp.

Article Title: 'Some good news': Two sisters of ex-Pak PM Imran Khan released from jail; elder sister, wife remain behind bars
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two sisters of Pakistan's incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan were released from a Lahore jail on Thursday after the Punjab government revoked their detention orders, leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) party said.However, his elder sister and wife remain behind bars."Finally, some good news. Two of former PM Imran Khan's sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, have been released from Kot Lakhpat Jail following the withdrawal of their detention orders," PTI senior leader and former federal minister Moonis Elahi said in a statement."Hopefully, Aleema sahiba and Bushra Bibi, will also be released soon," he added, referring to the cricketer-turned-politician's elder sister and wife, respectively.Meanwhile, another senior PTI leader, Zulfi Bokhari, asserted that the release of Imran Khan's two sisters would not "erase the suffering" endured by his family."The release of two sisters does not end the injustice or erase the suffering inflicted on Imran Khan’s family. The demand is clear -- no selective relief, no intimidation, and no further persecution," Bokhari told party supporters.Imran Khan's sisters were detained in September under a public safety law to prevent them from mobilising support for a nationwide protest demanding his release.Bushra Bibi was arrested in January 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced.The 74-year-old PTI founder has been in prison since 2023 and faces more than 100 cases, including corruption charges and allegations of inciting violence.On Wednesday, PTI lawyers met Imran Khan at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail to discuss his ongoing court cases, a day after the Islamabad high court directed authorities to facilitate the meeting.The lawyers spent four hours at the prison before leaving without speaking to the media.According to PTI lawyer Latif Khosa, who was part of the delegation, Imran Khan was experiencing problems with his blood pressure and eyesight.
Article Summary: Two sisters of Pakistan's incarcerated former PM Imran Khan were released from a Lahore jail on Thursday. The Punjab government revoked their detention orders, leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) party said. But his elder sister and wife remain behind bars.

Article Title: Pakistan announces schedule for Guru Nanak’s 557th birth anniversary celebrations despite Attari-Wagah closure
Article Text:
Pakistan has maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side (Photo: PTI).

AMRITSAR: Despite the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah international land border following Operation Sindoor, the Pakistan government has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev, expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib.Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side, although pilgrim movement through it continues to be suspended by India.According to Pak media reports, the programme was finalised at a meeting of the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (PSGPC), chaired by its president and Punjab provincial minister for minority affairs and human rights, Ramesh Singh Arora, to review arrangements for the celebrations.As per the schedule, Indian Sikh pilgrims are expected to arrive in Pakistan through the Attari international border on November 22. The main ceremony will be held on November 24 at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev. The pilgrims are scheduled to return on December 1.Reacting to Pakistan’s announcement, Sikh scholar Jagdeep Singh said the proposed pilgrimage programme assumes significance amid strained India-Pakistan ties and the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah border after Operation Sindoor.“Keeping the border open would serve the interests of both countries and, above all, make it easier for devotees to visit their historic religious shrines,” said Jagdeep.Interestingly, while Pakistan maintains that the Kartarpur corridor is operational on its side and has expressed readiness to facilitate Sikh devotees, India has suspended pilgrim movement through it since May 2025.In a statement, Arora said Pakistani diplomatic missions had been instructed to facilitate visa issuance for Sikh pilgrims. He also urged India to allow the Sikh sangat to visit its historic shrines.According to reports, the arrangements reviewed at the meeting include air-conditioned buses, accommodation, langar, medical facilities, mineral water and currency exchange services. A Rescue 1122 ambulance will accompany every convoy of 20 buses to meet medical emergencies.
Article Summary: Pakistan has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev. It is expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib. Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side.

Article Title: 'Two eight-year-olds or four four-year-olds': Pakistani cleric's child bride 'joke' sparks outrage
Article Text:
Mufti Tariq Masood (Source: Wikimedia Commons)

Education and women's autonomy

Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood, who commands a large following across social media platforms, has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage.In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.One of the remarks highlighted in the report came from a viral video in which Masood joked that if someone could not find a 16-year-old bride, he could provide “two eight-year-olds” or “four four-year-olds”. The comment drew criticism from people who said it trivialised child marriage and normalised the sexualisation of minors.The Daily Mirror said the backlash was dismissed by supporters as a misunderstanding, with the remark defended as a joke taken out of context.The newspaper also pointed to Masood's repeated opposition to statutory minimum marriage-age laws. According to the report, he has argued that Islamic jurisprudence does not prescribe a universal minimum age of 18 and that parents or guardians should retain discretion over when a girl marries.A recurring theme in his sermons, the newspaper said, is the emphasis on physical development and perceived maturity rather than chronological age when determining whether a girl is ready for marriage. The preacher had made remarks discussing the physical suitability of girls aged nine and ten in the context of marital relations. Pakistan as a country has been grappling with child sexual abuse, forced marriages and gender equality and positioning such leaders as popular figures raises extreme concerns.The Daily Mirror also highlighted Masood's remarks on women's education, saying that some of his statements appear to place a husband's authority above a young wife's decision to continue her studies.It further cited comments about women marrying late, including references to them becoming “aunties”, and discussions of the benefits husbands derive from marriage.Masood has also been criticised for presenting early marriage as a way to manage men's sexual desiresMasood's sermons have reportedly become difficult to access after copyright complaints and takedown requests. Critics have alleged that this limits public scrutiny of his statements, while his supporters maintain that some remarks are circulated without their original context.Masood has built a substantial following on YouTube, Facebook and other social media platforms through a preaching style that combines religious instruction with informal language and humour. His reach extends beyond traditional religious institutions, particularly among younger and urban audiences.
Article Summary: Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage. In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.

Article Title: Pakistan militant attack kills 10 policemen in KPK's Kohat, gunbattle still under way
Article Text:
No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. (FIle photo)

At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Wednesday, officials told news agency AP.The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire between the attackers and security forces, local police official Faisal Khan said.Khan confirmed that two senior police officers were among those killed. He added that the gunbattle was still underway, but did not share further details.No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. However, suspicion is likely to centre on the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, which has intensified its attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.Pakistan has witnessed a rise in militant violence over the past few years, with much of it attributed to the TTP. The group is separate from the Afghan Taliban but shares close ties with it. The Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.Islamabad has repeatedly accused Afghanistan's Taliban-led government of providing shelter to TTP fighters operating against Pakistan. Kabul has denied the allegations.
Article Summary: At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire. No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far.

Article Title: Pakistan court frames charges against 8, including grandson of deputy PM Ishaq Dar, in gang rape case
Article Text:
Pakistan deput​y PM Ishaq Dar (File photo)​​

A Pakistani court on Wednesday framed charges against eight suspects, including the grandson of deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, in connection with the gang rape of two foreign women , an official said.All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty, the official added.“Lahore court judge Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty. He directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on December 9 so that the formal trial proceedings could begin,” the official said.Earlier, police in Pakistan's Punjab province had cleared Raza Dar and his four accomplices of charges in the case, instead charging three other employees of Ishaq Dar's grandson of raping the women.The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela. They were allegedly kidnapped and raped by Raza Dar and his four friends after arriving in Lahore on a business trip in June. Medical examinations confirmed that the women had been raped. They returned to their respective countries after recording their statements.According to the police report, the women met Raza Dar in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest in their cryptocurrency business.After receiving returns on his initial investment, he invested more than $500,000. However, the women allegedly failed to provide further returns or repay the amount.In June, Raza Dar invited the women to Pakistan on the pretext of arranging a meeting with another investor. They initially stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to the hill station of Murree voluntarily.The women were later taken to a house in Lahore's Defence Housing Authority, where they were allegedly held captive and pressured to repay the money. They were forced to transfer $19,500, as per the police report.Armed men guarded the women and threatened them with a knife, a gun and a broken piece of mirror. They also threatened to kill them and sell their body parts if they failed to meet the demands.The women eventually managed to escape after the vehicle in which their alleged captors were taking them to Lahore airport met with an accident.
Article Summary: Pakistani court frames charges against eight suspects in gang rape of two foreign women. All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty. The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela.

Article Title: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan taken to hospital for eye check-up, treatment; shifted back to Adiala Jail
Article Text:
Imran Khan's health sparks concern

Qureshi also hospitalised

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison, news agency Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing officials.Khan, who is lodged in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, was taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), where he also received treatment for blood pressure-related issues, one of the officials said."He had some blood pressure issues ... and was given required treatment last night. He has been shifted back to his prison cell," the person said.The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years after losing power in a no-confidence vote in 2022. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging that they are politically motivated. The Shehbaz Sharif government has rejected his claims.All but one of Khan's convictions have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending.His lawyers have repeatedly raised concerns over his health in prison, claiming that his condition has deteriorated and that he has lost significant vision in his right eye.Wednesday's hospital visit is the first known instance of Khan being taken for treatment and subsequently returned to jail since August, when an earlier hospital visit was cut short.Meanwhile, a Pakistani court has directed jail authorities to allow Khan's legal team to meet him and his wife, his party said.Khan's hospital visit comes a day after his close aide and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) deputy chairman, Shah Mahmood Qureshi, was taken to a hospital in Lahore after collapsing inside his barrack at Kot Lakhpat Jail.According to a prison official, Qureshi suffered a dizzy spell while walking inside his barrack on Monday, injuring his knee and arm in the fall.The 70-year-old former foreign minister was subsequently shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology for treatment and remains hospitalised.Khan, who led Pakistan to its maiden ODI World Cup title in 1992, has been behind bars for more than three years. Concerns over his health and prison conditions have repeatedly been raised by his family, party members and supporters, including former international cricket colleagues.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison. The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging they are politically motivated.

Article Title: More debt, less development? Pakistan spends just 10% of annual budget
Article Text: More debt, less development? Pakistan spends just 10% of annual budget
Article Summary: Pakistan spends just 10% of its annual budget on development, according to a report. The report says the country has more debt than any other country in the world. Pakistan is one of the most debt-ridden countries in the Western world, the report says.

Article Title: Imran Khan aide, ex-Pakistan foreign minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi collapses in jail; hospitalised
Article Text:
(With PTI inputs)

Pakistan's former foreign minister and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf vice-chairman Shah Mahmood Qureshi was admitted to a hospital after collapsing in his barrack at a jail in Lahore, a prison official said on Tuesday.According to the official, Qureshi suffered a dizzy spell while walking inside his barrack at Kot Lakhpat Jail on Monday, injuring his knee and arm in the fall.The 70-year-old leader was subsequently shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology for treatment, the official added.Qureshi has been in jail since August 2023 in multiple cases linked to the May 9, 2023, riots, when Tehreek-i-Insaf supporters went on a rampage following the arrest of party chairman and former Prime Minister Imran Khan.Qureshi's counsel, Rana Mudassar Umar, confirmed that the veteran politician was taken to hospital after fainting and suffering a fall.Umar added that the PTI leader would remain under observation for 24 hours, after which doctors would decide whether he should continue treatment at the hospital or be shifted back to jail.Meanwhile, Qureshi's daughter alleged that her father had been jailed on "trumped-up" charges and accused the federal government of keeping him behind bars with "malafide" intent."Three and a half years ago, a hale and hearty lion heart was sent to jail on trumped-up charges. He not only fought the cypher case with resolve and courage but refused to sacrifice his principles at the altar of self-interest," Mehr Bano said."My father has been acquitted multiple times but remains behind bars due to the government's malafide. Over 90 bail hearings have gone by, but the record has yet to be produced. A man whose innocence has been proven again and again is being held... It is high time the judge establishes his authority and grants him bail," she demanded.Bano also highlighted her father's more than four decades of public service in Pakistan."He has served twice as Pakistan's foreign minister, and as parliamentary leader and vice-chairman of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, he has fulfilled important responsibilities and protected Pakistan's interests. He has fought for the supremacy of the Constitution and democracy. He deserves justice and freedom," she stated.
Article Summary: Pakistan's former foreign minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi was admitted to a hospital after collapsing in his barrack at a jail in Lahore. The 70-year-old has been in jail since August 2023 in multiple cases linked to the May 9, 2023, riots. His daughter has accused the federal government of keeping him behind bars with "malafide" intent.

Article Title: Lashkar terrorist Hafiz Saeed's political outfit loses Pakistan's parliamentary bypoll
Article Text:
Terrorist Hafiz Saeed was previously associated with the Milli Muslim League.

A political party linked to Mumbai terror attack mastermind Hafiz Saeed has suffered a defeat in a parliamentary by-election in Pakistan, with the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) retaining the seat.The contest took place on Sunday in the NA-77 constituency of Gujranwala district in Punjab, around 80 km from Lahore. The by-election was necessitated by the death of sitting lawmaker Mehmood Bashir Virk.According to results announced by the Election Commission on Monday, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) candidate Muhammad Ibrahim Gujjar secured more than 30,000 votes. However, he was defeated by PML-N's Rashid Bashir Virk, who polled over 43,000 votes.The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, the Pakistan Peoples Party and Jamaat-e-Islami did not contest the by-election.The polling saw a low voter turnout and was accompanied by allegations of electoral malpractice. Voters in one village boycotted the election entirely, while five PML-N women lawmakers were issued notices seeking explanations over alleged violations of the election code of conduct.Rejecting the outcome, the PMML accused the ruling PML-N of widespread rigging and refused to accept the results.The party had also contested Pakistan's 2024 general elections but failed to win a single seat.Hafiz Saeed, who founded the banned terrorist outfits Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jamaat-ud-Dawa, was previously associated with the Milli Muslim League. The PMML later emerged as another political platform linked to him and reportedly enjoys the backing of Pakistan's establishment.
Article Summary: The contest took place on Sunday in the NA-77 constituency of Gujranwala district in Punjab, around 80 km from Lahore. The by-election was necessitated by the death of sitting lawmaker Mehmood Bashir Virk. Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) candidate Muhammad Ibrahim Gujjar secured more than 30,000 votes.

Article Title: Pakistani TV anchor Rabia Ahsan shot dead at home; police probe husband's claim of accidental firing
Article Text:
Pakistani TV anchorperson Rabia Ahsan shot dead at home in Rawalpindi

First Lady condemns killing, calls for transparent probe

A Pakistani television anchorperson, Rabia Ahsan, was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on Sunday, with police taking her husband into custody and seizing the suspected weapon, Pakistani media outlet Samaa reported.The incident took place in the Gulshanabad area of the city, where Ahsan worked as an anchor and programme host for a local private TV channel.City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera confirmed that Ahsan's husband had been detained and that the suspected weapon had been seized. He said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding her death.According to the CPO, a male domestic worker at the house told police that Ahsan's husband had claimed the gunshot was fired accidentally.Sukhera visited the crime scene along with the senior superintendent of police (SSP) operations, the SSP investigations and a team of forensic experts. Teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) were collecting evidence from the house.The body was being taken to a hospital for a postmortem examination. Sukhera said a case was being registered and the investigation would be conducted on merit.Pakistan's First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari expressed deep sadness over Ahsan's killing and strongly condemned the violence.She called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible were held accountable, according to a statement issued by the Presidency.Bhutto-Zardari also expressed concern over what she described as a “disturbing pattern of killing of another professional woman in the same metropolitan area”.She recalled the murder of Hina Javed, a 45-year-old digital media executive who was found dead at her Rawalpindi residence in August with signs of torture.The First Lady noted that the outcome of the investigation into Javed's murder was still awaited.
Article Summary: Rabia Ahsan was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on Sunday. Police took her husband into custody and seized the suspected weapon. Pakistan's First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari condemned the killing.

Article Title: Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans faceless anti-terror courts: Report
Article Text:
Faceless terror courts, Rs 70bn police boost planned in Pakistan’s KP (Reuters photo)

Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province plans to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts to protect witnesses, prosecutors and judges involved in terrorism cases, according to a report by Dawn on Sunday.The provincial administration also plans to allocate 70 billion Pakistani rupees annually to the police and Counter-Terrorism Department to strengthen their capabilities, the report said.The developments come less than a month after Pakistan's federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, accusing the provincial government led by former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of failing to engage in the fight against terrorism.Under the move, the chief minister and provincial cabinet ceased to hold office, with Governor Faisal Karim Kundi assuming executive authority with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council.Both the national assembly and senate approved the emergency on October 14, while a joint sitting of Parliament endorsed the emergency and governor's rule the following day.At a televised briefing on Sunday, Home Secretary Amjad Ali Khan said an amendment had been sent to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts.He said witnesses were reluctant to testify in terrorism cases because of fears for their safety. The proposed system would also protect prosecutors and judges, *Dawn* quoted him as saying.Khan said the administration planned to allocate 59.8 billion Pakistani rupees to the police and 10.3 billion Pakistani rupees to the Counter-Terrorism Department, with funds earmarked for infrastructure and equipment.The plans also include strengthening police stations and checkpoints, expanding the Safe City project and installing anti-drone systems in Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat and Bannu, the report said.Khan said the province faced a shortage of more than 10,000 police personnel and lacked adequate security infrastructure, particularly in the merged districts. He also flagged weak counter-drone capabilities, noting that militants were increasingly using drone technology.The administration plans to intensify intelligence-based operations, arrest terrorist facilitators, re-verify people placed on Pakistan's Fourth Schedule and mobilise the Rapid Response Force, Khan said.It also plans to deploy artificial intelligence tools to monitor social media and counter terrorist narratives, while satellite communication systems will be installed in areas with inadequate connectivity.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor Kundi, who attended the briefing, said restoring peace and strengthening the police were the administration's priorities. He said development could follow only after security was restored and called for greater political ownership of the fight against terrorism.Kundi said the police would be provided with weapons, ammunition and other resources, while facilities in the merged districts would also be improved. He said groups taking up arms against the state could not be offered dialogue and would be dealt with accordingly, Dawn reported.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province plans to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts to protect witnesses, prosecutors and judges involved in terrorism cases. The provincial administration also plans to allocate 70 billion Pakistani rupees annually to the police and Counter-Terrorism Department.

Article Title: Balochistan Parties call statewide shutdown in mid-November as crisis deepens in troubled province
Article Text:
(Representative image) (Photo: ANI).

Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19, to be followed by demonstrations at district headquarters. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns.The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP) at the Quetta Press Club, according to a report by The Express Tribune cited by ANI. ANP provincial president Asghar Khan Achakzai chaired the meeting, which was attended by representatives of the National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Pashtunkhwa National Awami Party and several other political groups. The participants agreed to bring their joint political and democratic efforts under a coordinated movement to raise public grievances.In a joint declaration, the parties described the situation in Balochistan as alarming. They cited persistent insecurity, terrorism, extremism, armed group activities, targeted killings and kidnappings for ransom. They also raised the unresolved issue of missing persons, and highlighted the difficulties faced by transporters and passengers travelling on national highways.The parties pointed to rising unemployment and economic decline. They blamed the closure of trade and transit routes with Afghanistan and Iran for disrupting economic activity across the province. Soaring inflation, prolonged power and gas outages, petroleum levies and restrictions on the supply of essential agricultural inputs, including urea fertiliser, were also cited. According to The Express Tribune, the leaders said these issues had adversely affected agriculture, trade, industries and employment.The participating parties also criticised the provincial and federal governments, accusing them of failing to ensure public safety, maintain law and order, protect natural resources and restore economic stability.Furthermore, the parties announced a provincial-level meeting on November 26 to decide the next course of action. An all-parties conference will be held in the first week of December to take Balochistan’s concerns to the national leadership.
Article Summary: Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns. The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP)

Article Title: 'If he wishes to come’: Pakistan open to considering visa for Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s Lahore visit
Article Text:
पंजाब सीएम भगवंत मान

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann should visit Pakistan for the World Punjabi Conference? Yes, it would promote cultural ties. No, travel could be risky. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27, following an invitation to the event.Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing while responding to a question about Mann's possible visit, PTI reported."The government would consider issuing Mann a visa if he wishes to visit Pakistan. However, whether the Indian government permits him to travel is an entirely separate matter," he told reporters in Islamabad.On October 23, Mann had said that he had received an invitation to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore.However, the Punjab chief minister also raised doubts over whether he would be permitted to travel to Pakistan.“Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he remarked.Mann had also voiced his wish for all members of the Punjab legislative assembly to visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if it reopened.The corridor, which links Dera Baba Nanak in Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims visiting the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.It enables Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without a Pakistani visa, subject to applicable arrangements.The corridor has remained closed to pilgrims travelling from the India since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22.Last month, the Centre denied political clearance to Mann for his visit to Paris, prompting the Punjab government to challenge the decision before the Punjab and Haryana high court.The high court subsequently cleared his visit, observing that the Centre had “not explained” the political considerations it cited while refusing permission for his trip to the French capital.
Article Summary: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27. Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing.

Article Title: Ties strained, India-Bangladesh consular talks postponed
Article Text:
Ties strained, India-Bangladesh consular talks postponed

DHAKA: The fifth Bangladesh-India consular dialogue - scheduled to be held in Dhaka on Nov 17-18 - has been postponed, indicating that bilateral mechanisms between the two countries appear to have stalled, with little tangible progress on key areas of cooperation.The dialogue was supposed to discuss former PM Sheikh Hasina's extradition, cross-border issues, border management, streamlining visa processes, repatriating citizens detained in either country, securing the release and repatriation of fishermen, and fostering mutual legal cooperation.On Nov 3, an inter-ministerial meeting was held at the ministry of foreign affairs in Dhaka as part of preparation for the consular dialogue between the two countries.The fourth round of consular dialogue was held on May 29, 2024, in New Delhi.
Article Summary: The fifth Bangladesh-India consular dialogue was scheduled to be held in Dhaka on Nov 17-18. The dialogue was supposed to discuss former PM Sheikh Hasina's extradition, cross-border issues, border management, streamlining visa processes.

Chinese vloggers accused of defaming India by filming poor neighbourhoods in Dhaka and falsely portraying the footage as scenes from New Delhi have "scaled down" their activities following increased surveillance by local law enforcement agencies, a Bangladeshi police official said.The authorities stepped up monitoring of the Chinese nationals, around 150 in number, after India expressed concern over the alleged use of Bangladeshi territory to tarnish its image.According to Mohammad Khalid Mansur, officer-in-charge of Dhaka’s Uttara West Police Station, intelligence agencies intensified surveillance of the Chinese nationals and began monitoring them closely. This led to a decline in their activities, the newspaper Prothom Alo reported on Thursday.Earlier, Bangladeshi media reports said the Chinese vloggers were active in Dhaka’s Tekpara and Uttara neighbourhoods, livestreaming footage of narrow streets and impoverished localities on Chinese social media platforms. They are accused of misrepresenting these areas as parts of New Delhi and making "disparaging" comments about the residents’ living conditions.The vloggers filmed people’s homes and everyday activities, at times entering residential premises without permission.Residents were unaware of where the footage was being uploaded or how they were being portrayed.The activities are suspected to be part of a coordinated disinformation campaign.“There was no police surveillance of their activities. More than 100 vloggers were making such videos every day. They also paid Bangladeshi citizens to assist them in this work,” Prothom Alo reported.On Tuesday, the ministry of external affairs in New Delhi called for appropriate action against the vloggers for peddling "false narratives" to defame India.Following the controversy, the Chinese nationals were asked to produce their passports and visas and explain why they were engaging in such activities while visiting Bangladesh on tourist visas.Police also instructed them to leave the country upon the expiry of their authorised stay.However, it remains unclear whether a formal investigation has been initiated into their activities or whether any action has been taken over possible violations of visa conditions.Residents, meanwhile, reported that they had not seen any Chinese nationals in Uttara or Tekpara over the past few days."I have been at home for two days due to illness and have not seen any Chinese citizens around," Md Selim, a Tekpara resident, told the newspaper.Rickshaw puller Imamul Islam described a bridge over a canal near Sector 12 in Uttara as a "hideout" for the Chinese vloggers."They would film us throughout the day and night, including our passengers. I haven't seen them around for some time now," he added.
Article Summary: Chinese vloggers accused of defaming India by filming poor neighbourhoods in Dhaka and falsely portraying footage as scenes from New Delhi. Authorities stepped up monitoring of the Chinese nationals, around 150 in number, after India expressed concern over the alleged use of Bangladeshi territory to tarnish its image.

Article Title: Political activities must be open to all in Bangladesh: UN
Article Text:
Political activities must be open to all in B’desh: UN

DHAKA: The United Nations (UN) has said "all political parties and political personalities" of Bangladesh should be free to participate in political activities, amid street violence and protests in the capital and other parts of the country, events that coincide with former PM Sheikh Hasina 's proposed return from exile next month.Dhaka has claimed that the protests are being led by supporters of Hasina's banned Awami League, its student outfit Chhatra League and organisations linked to them. Since Monday, dozens of crude bombs have exploded, and passenger vehicles have been set on fire in Dhaka and other districts, leaving one person dead and several injured. At least 18 branches of Grameen Bank - a microfinance organisation founded by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, who served as head of the interim govt formed after Hasina's ouster in 2024 - have come under attack across Bangladesh in the past two weeks, with two offices targeted in the last 24 hours."Certainly, regarding political activity, we believe that all political parties and all political personalities should be free to participate," Farhan Haq, deputy spokesman for the UN secretary-general, told reporters in New York on Tuesday.
Article Summary: U.N. says "all political parties and political personalities" of Bangladesh should be free to participate in political activities. Comes amid street violence and protests in the capital and other parts of the country. Events coincide with former PM Sheikh Hasina's proposed return from exile next month.
